rationale: Round 0 built and ran correctly with no ICE, so the table is shifted toward stronger obfuscation rather than conservatism. FLA gets the highest SecurityGain (0.80) since control-flow flattening is the strongest structural defense and this program's largest function (test_lists, 899 of 1686 text bytes) is a good flattening target; its RuntimeCost/CorrectnessRisk weights stay mid-range so hot numeric loops (heapsort, matrix, ary3, sieve) are not flattened indiscriminately. SUB and ICALL stay high on SecurityGain because arithmetic substitution and indirect calls are cheap-to-moderate semantic disruptions that pair well with flattening; ICALL's CorrectnessRisk remains 0.30 to keep it off fragile indirect-call sites in methcall/objinst. BCF and IBR get moderate weights to add opaque predicates and branch injection without compounding runtime blowup on loop-heavy shootout kernels. SPLIT and IGV are the low-risk complements: SPLIT divides the few larger functions to increase FLA/SUB surface at near-zero runtime cost, and IGV keeps DiversityGain high (0.80) since global variable renaming plus new global variables uniquely frustrates static pattern matching in this small-binary setting. Overall the cost dimensions (0.20-0.50) permit aggressive selection on cold functions while gating the hottest loops, and no pass is disabled given the clean round-0 result.
